question: What will be the percentage change in the FTSE 100 index (^FTSE on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-09-21 to the close on 2026-10-02?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-10-02 / close on 2026-09-21 - 1), using daily closes of ^FTSE on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-10-02, the last close before it is used.
research:
I couldn't open Yahoo Finance or most article pages directly (the proxy refused the connection), so the figures below come from search-result summaries of the cited pages. The 21 Sep starting value has not been confirmed on Yahoo. As of the 22 Sep close the index was down about 0.13% from that value, which settles nothing.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on Yahoo Finance ^FTSE daily closes: 100 x (close on 2026-10-02 / close on 2026-09-21 - 1). I could not load the [Yahoo history page](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EFTSE/history/).
- 2026-09-21: the FTSE 100 reportedly closed at **10,739.01**, up 0.75% (+79.88 points). The day's range was about 10,656.70 to 10,774.66. [BBN Times](https://www.bbntimes.com/global-economy/ftse-100-today-london-closes-at-10-739-01-up-0-75-as-miners-and-banks-outweigh-oil-weakness); the same figure appears in the [Hilsden 22 Sep note](https://hilsdentrading.substack.com/p/ftse100-analysis-for-22nd-september-7fe).
- Investing.com's table shows a row of about 10,738.97 dated 22-09-2026. Its columns don't agree with each other, so it may be a date or row mix-up. [Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/indices/uk-100-historical-data)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-09-22: the FTSE 100 closed at **10,725.48** (-13.53, -0.13%), per LSEG data. The FTSE 250 rose 0.53% to 24,622.29. [Lemming Investor snapshot](https://lemminginvestor.substack.com/p/london-market-snapshot-tuesday-22)
- That leaves the index about -0.13% from the 21 Sep base, with 8 trading sessions left (23 Sep to 2 Oct).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-21: miners, banks and industrials outweighed weakness in BP and Shell as Brent fell below $100. [BBN Times](https://www.bbntimes.com/global-economy/ftse-100-today-london-closes-at-10-739-01-up-0-75-as-miners-and-banks-outweigh-oil-weakness)
- 2026-09-21: the quarterly review changes took effect. Easyjet and Ithaca Energy joined the index; Entain and Persimmon left. [LSEG](https://www.lseg.com/en/media-centre/press-releases/2026/ftse-uk-index-series-review-september-2026)
- 2026-09-21: a market preview said oil prices were easing but Bank of England rate risks remain. [Sunday Guardian](https://sundayguardianlive.com/business/uk-stock-market-forecast-today-september-21-2026-ftse-100-expected-to-open-higher-today-as-oil-prices-ease-bank-of-england-rate-risks-persist-289412/)
- 2026-09-18: the index fell about 1.4-1.5% to roughly 10,652-10,659, led by banks (Barclays and Lloyds each about -2.5%). Sources disagree on the exact close. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-kingdom/stock-market/news/585083); [Kitco/Reuters](https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-09-18/londons-ftse-100-retreats-banks-energy-weigh-eyes-weekly-rise)
- 2026-09-16/17: the Bank of England held rates at 3.75% on a 6-3 vote, with three members wanting a hike to 4%. UK CPI was 3.1% in August, and the Bank expects about 3.75% in Q4 2026. Brent was about $106 on 14 Sep, linked to the Middle East conflict. [MTS Insights](https://www.mtsinsights.com/summaries/10990/)
- 2026-09-04: the FTSE was flat around 10,834, with Brent near $96. [Invezz](https://invezz.com/news/2026/09/04/why-is-the-ftse-100-stuck-near-flat-even-as-wall-street-and-oil-prices-rally/); [Analytics Insight](https://www.analyticsinsight.net/stocks/ftse-100-live-index-opened-flat-at-1083477-ahead-of-us-non-farm-payroll-report-brent-at-usd-9554)

## 4. Base rates
- The 52-week range is 9,276.91 to 10,989.45, so the index is about 2.4% below its 52-week high. [Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/indices/uk-100-historical-data)
- The window is 9 trading sessions (21 Sep close to 2 Oct close). My own estimate, not from a source: with annualised volatility of 12-16%, one standard deviation over 9 sessions is roughly 2.3-3.0%. About two thirds of comparable windows would fall within ±2.5-3%, and moves beyond ±5% are rare outside crisis periods.
- Recent daily moves have been large: -1.5% on 18 Sep and +0.75% on 21 Sep. That points to volatility at or above the usual level, driven mainly by oil.
- Historically, the long-run average drift over two weeks is small, about +0.2-0.3%.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets on the FTSE 100 for this window.
- I found no published sell-side targets for early October 2026. In mid-August, a Reuters poll of economists expected the Bank of England to hold through year end, while Goldman Sachs and Citi saw a hike by end-2026. [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/news/economists-agree-boe-will-hold-rates-through-year-end-reuters-poll-202608181809); [IDN Financials](https://www.idnfinancials.com/news/68857/citi-goldman-sachs-see-boe-raising-interest-rates)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Oil and the Middle East:** Brent's swings around $100 move BP and Shell (positively) and drive rate expectations (negatively). [MTS Insights](https://www.mtsinsights.com/summaries/10990/)
- **Late September:** I'm going on the usual calendar here, not a confirmed schedule. US PCE inflation is due around 25-26 Sep, and the final UK Q2 GDP release around 30 Sep.
- **2026-10-02 (resolution day):** the US September jobs report is normally due that morning, US time, before the London close. Recent payroll surprises have moved the FTSE. [Yahoo UK](https://uk.news.yahoo.com/ftse-100-live-focus-us-064103402.html)
- **Banks:** speculation about a Bank of England hike at the 5 Nov meeting could keep weighing on bank shares.
- **Quarter-end rebalancing:** on 30 Sep. The September index changes are already in effect.
